info.title: viggle/motion-capture
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "viggle/motion-capture", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. `x-comfy-router-input-modalities` records the media kinds the model is documented to accept; the request schema is shared across sibling models and may admit media kinds this model ignores. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description: Router body of a Viggle 3D animation captured from a video.

motion_video_url.description: Public http(s) URL of a video of a person moving, up to 100 MiB.

smooth_velocity_threshold.description: Velocity threshold of the smoothing. Only with `enable_smoothing`.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description: Comfy Router output schema for Viggle 3D animations: the ready `GET /proxy/viggle/v1/motions/{motion_id}/files` document. `glb` and `fbx` each carry a skeleton for the Mixamo, MetaHuman and MetaHuman Body rigs. The URLs are Viggle's and expire after one hour.

ViggleError.description: Viggle's error object, set when the job failed.

ViggleMotionFiles.description: A Viggle 3D animation and, once ready, its files.

credits_used.description: Viggle credits the job is charged, set once it is ready.

status.description: Status: queued, processing, ready or failed.

ViggleMotionRigFiles.description: Download URLs of one file format, one per rig.
